title: Using TOGAF with Other Frameworks, and Applying Iteration to the ADM

blocks.text: SESSION 1 — Concept · Key Points · Memory Technique. Read, absorb, stop.
1. Concept Explained Simply

**TOGAF with Other Frameworks**: No organisation adopts TOGAF into a vacuum — they already run ITIL, PRINCE2/PMBOK, COBIT, and Agile methods. TOGAF focuses on defining architecture deliverables and method; most other frameworks are relatively silent on architecture method — exactly the gap TOGAF fills. TOGAF integrates with these frameworks rather than replacing them.

**Applying Iteration to the ADM**: The sequential phase presentation "can be read to imply a deterministic waterfall methodology" — but this is a communication convenience, not a mandate. In practice, organisations apply the ADM through three types of iteration and choose different classes of engagement depending on the work needed.
2a. Key Points — TOGAF with Other Frameworks

Two key elements of any EA framework: a definition of deliverables, and a description of method. Most frameworks focus on the first; TOGAF provides the second — a flexible content framework whose generic deliverables can be replaced or extended by another framework's.
Frameworks TOGAF integrates with: ITIL, CMMI, COBIT, PRINCE2, PMBOK, MSP — plus TOGAF Library materials like IT4IT.

**Architectural Styles**: Addressing a distinctive style should NOT require significant changes to TOGAF itself — it adjusts the models, viewpoints, and tools selected in Phases B, C, D. Dominance of a style may direct a revisit to the Preliminary Phase.
**Enterprise Agility**: Broader than Agile software development. TOGAF embraces responsiveness through Partitions (how work is broken down) and Levels (granularity) — see Lesson 20.
2b. Key Points — Applying Iteration to the ADM
Three types of iteration:

rows: Multiple ADM cycles, each bound by its own Request for Architecture Work, populate/extend the Architecture Landscape. Concurrent projects; one may trigger another.
Phases run concurrently, loop in planned cycles, or are revisited to update work products with new information.
A new pass through the Preliminary Phase — triggered by Phase A needs OR a Phase H Change Request.

blocks.text: Four Iteration Cycles: Architecture Capability (mobilise) → Architecture Development (create BDAT content) → Transition Planning (roadmap) → Architecture Governance (oversee delivery).

Three Classes of Engagement: Identification of Required Change (broad, strategic visibility) · Definition of Change (Foundational or Bounded initiatives) · Implementation of Change (governance of delivery).
**Foundational vs Bounded**: Foundational = known objective but NOT strictly scoped by a shared vision (understand the problem first). Bounded = outcome already agreed (elaborate a solution).
Baseline First vs Target First:

rows: Baseline is complex, unclear, or not agreed — common with high business unit autonomy
Target agreed at a high level; baseline is broadly understood — faster, avoids perpetuating sub-optimal baseline patterns

blocks.text: 3. Memory Technique

Three iteration types — "Landscape, Cycle, Capability." Four iteration cycles — "CDGT": Capability → Development → Transition Planning → Governance.

Baseline First vs Target First trigger question: "Is the current state a mess or well understood?" Mess → Baseline First. Understood → Target First.
EXAM TRAP 1 — SEQUENTIAL PRESENTATION ≠ MANDATE. The Standard explicitly warns its own phase-by-phase presentation "can be read to imply" waterfall — this is a communication convenience only.
EXAM TRAP 2 — FOUNDATIONAL ≠ SMALLER/SIMPLER. Foundational means the problem itself isn't yet well-defined — not that the initiative is small.
EXAM TRAP 3 — CAPABILITY ITERATION HAS TWO TRIGGERS. A Request for Architecture Work needing capability not yet established, OR a Change Request from Phase H. Not only at the very start.
✋ PAUSE POINT — CHECK BEFORE CONTINUING. Answer from memory before reading Session 2.
1. Why does TOGAF integrate with ITIL, COBIT, PRINCE2 rather than compete with them?

Most EA frameworks focus on deliverables but are silent on method. TOGAF provides that method as a flexible, extensible framework. Other frameworks' deliverables can replace or extend TOGAF's generic ones; the architect tailors TOGAF to integrate with existing processes.
2. Name the three types of iteration in the ADM.

(1) Landscape iteration — multiple ADM cycles, concurrent projects. (2) Within-cycle iteration — phases run concurrently, loop, or are revisited. (3) Capability iteration — a new Preliminary Phase pass, triggered by Phase A needs or a Phase H Change Request.
3. What's the difference between Baseline First and Target First, and when is each used?

Baseline First — assess current state first; used when baseline is complex/unclear/not agreed. Target First — elaborate target then map back; used when target is agreed and baseline is broadly understood.
SESSION 2 — Real-World Example · How It Works in Practice · Practice Questions · Part 2 Scenario
4. Real-World Example — GlobalTech Dynamics 365

**Framework integration**: ITIL — Architecture Compliance review timed to align with ITIL's Change Advisory Board process. PRINCE2 — Statement of Architecture Work mapped directly onto the PRINCE2 Project Initiation Document, avoiding a new document type.

**Classes of engagement**: Establishing the EA practice (L25) = Identification of Required Change (Supporting Business Strategy). The Dynamics 365 migration itself = Bounded Change Initiative — outcome (replace SAP, 20% cost reduction) already agreed before the ADM cycle began. Phase G governance throughout = Implementation of Change.

**Baseline First vs Target First applied**: Finance domain (L12) used Target First — Dynamics 365 Finance is a standard, well-understood module. The data quality problem (L13, 23% duplicates) required Baseline First for that specific workstream — the actual state of customer data was poorly understood.

**Capability iteration in practice**: The APRA regulation change (L17) triggered a new Preliminary Phase iteration — adjusting the Architecture Capability to add a Data Sovereignty Compliance Assessment process (also referenced in L25) — a textbook Phase H-triggered Capability iteration.
5. How It Actually Works in Practice
REALITY CHECK: EVERYBODY ITERATES, FEW DOCUMENT IT FORMALLY. Naming which type of iteration you're doing turns "we're just being pragmatic" into a structured, defensible justification to governance.

REALITY CHECK: BASELINE FIRST VS TARGET FIRST IS OFTEN CHOSEN UNCONSCIOUSLY. Different architects have different instinctive biases. Making the choice explicit — matched to the actual state of baseline understanding — resolves team friction quickly.
6. Part 1 Practice Questions
Q1. Which best describes the relationship between TOGAF and frameworks like ITIL, COBIT, PRINCE2?

items: A) TOGAF replaces these frameworks entirely
B) TOGAF defines architecture deliverables and method; designed to be tailored and integrated with these frameworks ✓
C) TOGAF cannot be used where these frameworks already exist
D) TOGAF and these frameworks have no overlap

blocks.text: Answer: B — TOGAF integrates with, not replaces, other frameworks.
Q2. What's the difference between a "Foundational" and "Bounded" change initiative?

items: A) Foundational is always smaller in scope
B) Foundational has a known objective but isn't strictly scoped by a shared vision (structure the problem first); Bounded has an agreed outcome (elaborate a solution) ✓
C) Bounded requires a new ADM cycle; Foundational doesn't
D) Foundational applies only to Business Architecture

blocks.text: Answer: B — the distinction is about how well-defined the outcome is, not scope size.
Q3. A Change Request during Phase H requires adjusting the Architecture Capability. What happens next?

items: A) Implement directly within Phase H, no earlier phase revisited
B) A new iteration of the Preliminary Phase should be initiated ✓
C) Defer until the next full ADM cycle from Phase A
D) The Architecture Board must dissolve and reform

blocks.text: Answer: B — one of the two triggers for Architecture Capability iteration.
7. Part 2 Scenario Question (Exam-Authentic Format)

SCENARIO: GlobalTech is exploring consolidating three regional data centres into Azure. The CTO says: "We don't know what's running in each data centre in detail — minimal documentation across independently managed sites. But we know we want to end up fully in Azure."

rows: Use Target First since the target (Azure) is stated — elaborate it first, then map back. Misapplies the decision criteria — Target First requires the baseline to be understood, which it explicitly isn't here.

Use Baseline First — the baseline (undocumented, independently managed) is complex and unclear, exactly the trigger condition. Classify as a Foundational Change Initiative — although the target direction is known, the true nature/scope of the problem isn't yet understood. Best answer.
Use Target First, classify as Bounded since the CTO has a clear desired outcome. Conflates "has a target direction" with "Bounded" — the real complexity is in the unknown baseline.

Neither approach appropriate until a full new Preliminary Phase reassesses the entire Architecture Capability. Unnecessarily disruptive — confuses content decisions with Capability iteration, which is only needed if the capability itself is inadequate.
